players.product: Tier III / Tier IV colocation data centers in Australia

connects_to.relationship: Data-center colocation capacity for SharonAI's AI factories (primary supplier)

contracts.signal: SharonAI prospectus: NextDC Limited, which provides data center colocation services, is one of SharonAI's top 3 operational suppliers (the others: ASE Pty Ltd, an intermediary providing Equinix data centre colocation and network services, and Lenovo). On March 28, 2024 the group entered into a new data center agreement with NextDC in Melbourne for its first dedicated AI cluster (commercial operation began June 28, 2024); on November 3, 2025 it signed a capacity expansion agreement with NextDC to secure up to an additional 50 MW. SharonAI has access to up to 54MWs of data center capacity with NEXTDC, which it says is expected to be ready for deployment in 2026, plus a roadmap to ~1GW of land, power and shell.
contracts.units: up to 54MWs; expansion of up to an additional 50 MW

connects_to.relationship: Compute and storage equipment supply to SharonAI (Lenovo TruScale program)

contracts.signal: SharonAI prospectus: SharonAI has obtained its compute and storage equipment primarily from Lenovo; Lenovo Global Technology (Australia and New Zealand) provides hardware managed services and is one of its top 3 operational suppliers. On April 24, 2024 the group entered into a services agreement with Lenovo to accelerate AI operations growth, and on 12 March 2025 it entered a scope of work agreement with Lenovo Global Financial Services (Australia and New Zealand) for AUD$7.4m of computer and networking equipment on a lease over 5 years.

players.product: Neocloud GPU compute platform: sovereign AI factories in Australia and New Zealand running NVIDIA B300 / GB300 clusters (GPU-as-a-service, AI platform layers, high-performance storage); NVIDIA Cloud Partner

quarterly_data.signal: Prospectus customer concentration: SharonAI's top 3 customers constituted 99% of its 2024 revenue, in no particular order: Filecoin Network (decentralized storage network; no services or revenue from it after June 30, 2025), Vast.ai and Runpod.io (GPU aggregator websites; SharonAI has no direct contact with the aggregators' underlying customers).

Prospectus operations and results: as of September 30, 2025 SharonAI operated 432 GPUs, 195 CPUs and over 51 PB of storage out of three third-party co-location data centers in Australia. Q3 2025 revenue was $506,747 versus $159,000 (provision of GPU infrastructure services $506,414 versus $51,789), driven primarily by growth of the GPU cloud services segment; nine-month revenue $1,208,824 versus $171,800.
